While, yes, you can find the typical goodies like elephant trousers, incense, and wall hangings, there are so many more cool, independent boutiques and designers in Goa getting their start! After all, while you can get those baggy, colorful elephant pants, how often can you really where them once you’re back home? Below is an insider list of places where you can find some really beautiful items, stuff to make your friends jealous. and stuff you will actually be able to wear once you return to your everyday life! headings: From Clothes To Home Decor: 9 Stores In North Goa That We Love
Paper Boat Collective, Noapara, Penha De Franca
payload.text_excerpt: Don't Miss Shopping At These 9 Best Stores In North Goa | LBB, Goa Similar Guides Shopping Women's Western Wear Stores Women's Accessories Stores From Clothes To Home Decor: 9 Stores In North Goa That We Love By Heena 24423 Interested | 98K Views Looking for souvenirs? Rare art? Beach dresses? Anything that screams Goa? Well, after many a shopping sprees, we've curated a list of stores that keep calling us back. Read on to find out our favourite fashion, home decor & other stores in North Goa. Rangeela Rangeela, Assagao See On Map VISIT SITE Gunpowder's equally popular neighbour Rangeela is as much of a visual treat as it a treasure hunt. It stocks up on apparel, decor, furniture, jewellery, bags and other knick-knacks. The way everything's found a spot in this Goan villa evokes a sense of awe and wonder. payload.text_excerpt: The Most Stylish Boutiques & Designers in Goa – Best Pixel Design Search Menu Cart 0 The Most Stylish Boutiques & Designers in Goa June 13, 2021 The shopping scene here is different to the rest of India. While, yes, you can find the typical goodies like elephant trousers, incense, and wall hangings, there are so many more cool, independent boutiques and designers in Goa getting their start! After all, while you can get those baggy, colorful elephant pants, how often can you really where them once you’re back home? Below is an insider list of places where you can find some really beautiful items, stuff to make your friends jealous. and stuff you will actually be able to wear once you return to your everyday life! Boutiques & Designers in Goa TIA Tia founded her namesake brand to offer a beautifully designed chic line of women’s swimwear and clothing. She’s a one woman entrepreneur who sources sustainable material and has everything made locally. Last season she had a beautiful shop in Mandrem – Alchemy – shared with Fara Boutique, though next year they are not sure if they will be going ahead with the space. Even if you haven’t made it to Goa yet, have a look at her website as she does international deliveries! If you are in Goa keep an eye and ear out for any Alchemy pop ups! Tia was one of Rachel’s best friends in Goa, so if you’ve ever wondered about what she was wearing in India , you’ve probably heard of this brand countless of times! Space Tribe morphed into existance on the paradise beaches of Goa, India in the early 90's, a collaboration between brothers Olli & Miki Wisdom, & Richmond Headspace. Our aim? To turn our world into a tripped out circus party wonderland, based on Psy trance beats, our love of bright colours and optically twisted patterns, combined with the use of blacklights, a healthy dose of circus skills and just a pinch of Psychedelic! Normal is Boring We were blasting at the parties & high on life, loving the pulse of the emerging psy trance music scene. But the clothes we wanted to wear, that celebrated our individuality & our joy of life didn't exist. Somehow, a pair of jeans & a benetton t-shirt didn't come close. Created in Chaos Off to Bali where we made a few dozen pieces of very colourful clothes & some funky batik banners for ourselves and a few friends. Upon our return to Goa we discovered many people were inspired & wanted a piece of the action too, so our personal production turned into a small scale business. payload.text_excerpt: 76 Multi-Brand Retailers Worth Knowing Subscribe Sign in 76 Multi-Brand Retailers Worth Knowing Where to find the most interesting mix of brands, around the world. Angharad Jones Best Apr 16, 2026 ∙ Paid 43 3 Share Earlier this year, I wrote the small and independent brand index : a list that currently stands at 138 womenswear brands that are, you guessed it, small and/or independent. I wanted to shine a light on the brands that are doing things differently and offering something beyond the usual. It’s my most popular post to date, so it turns out you lot are craving that, too. On the back of that, I started to think about all the multi-brand retailers where I quite often unearth these brands. The usual suspects online (hello, Net-a-Porter ), but also the small ones in residential neighbourhoods or in places you wouldn’t think to look. Where the owners know their customers by their first names, and where you can find the kinds of brands that are hard to come by elsewhere. So, welcome to the multi-brand retailer index. Some are online-only, while most have a physical and online presence, and most have both men’s and women’s wear. The UK list is heavy, as that’s where I've spent most of my life, but there are also plenty of entries for mainland Europe, North America, and Australia & New Zealand (big thanks to the subscribers in my chat who contributed their favourites!). payload.text_excerpt: Fashion multi-brands store: How to communicate with consumers - The Korea Times Go to Top my times The Korea Times open notice search Fashion multi-brands store: How to communicate with consumers Listen Listen Text Size Print Published Oct 21, 2014 6:05 pm KST Updated Oct 21, 2014 6:05 pm KST L’eclaireur This is the second in a four-part monthly series on trends by trend-watcher Interfashion Planning. — ED. Victoria Kim By Victoria Kim The fashion industry has undergone rapid change in the past three years. We have witnessed fast-fashion retailing followed by a sudden prominence of SPA brands, and now we have an emergence of multi-brand select shops where fashion and lifestyle coexist together. We have also seen a change in retailing from online stores to offline. For example, Style Nanda, an online shopping mall, has opened an off-line store on the strength of its online business. In China, there is a growing demand of spot stores which cover hot fashion trends in each region. It means that select shops are becoming diversified and offer both online and off line services to customers. Multi-shop is not a new notion. Its retailing identity simply has been evolving from individual product and merchandising-based to B2C communications. This change derives from concerns over how to communicate better with customers. Luxury shopping in Goa has grown into its own experience, one that feels curated, design-led, and deeply connected to the state’s slower coastal rhythm. This isn’t mall culture. It isn’t high-street chaos. And it’s definitely not flea-market bargaining. It's a boutique. It’s thoughtful, and it’s built for people who like discovering pieces, not just buying them. If you’re looking for luxury shopping in Goa, here’s what you should expect and where to go. The shift began when second-home buyers, designers, artists, and long-stay travellers started spending extended time here. They weren’t looking for fast fashion. They were looking for craftsmanship. payload.text_excerpt: Vogue’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital | Vogue Skip to main content Your All Access Pass GET THE APP Travel Vogue ’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital By Talia Abbas February 6, 2025 Photo: Getty Images Save this story Save this story The legacy of the Antwerp Six looms large in the Belgian port city of the same name, drawing fashion obsessives from all over to explore the cobblestoned streets that the avant-garde collective of Dries Van Noten, Ann Demeulemeester, Dirk Van Saene, Walter Van Beirendonck, Dirk Bikkembergs, and Marina Yee once called home in the 1980s. And nearly four decades after the group’s debut, a new crop of influential designers is putting Antwerp back at the center of the fashion map, making it a must-visit for those eager to immerse themselves in the same artistic milieu. Pieter Mulier , Alaïa’s creative director, and Raf Simons , Prada’s co-creative director both consider Antwerp their home base. Matthieu Blazy , Chanel’s recently appointed artistic director, has also spent considerable time in Antwerp. But beyond the promise of a chance encounter with one of the industry’s leading names, the city is also home to up-and-coming labels—La Collection, Bernadette, and Julie Kegels —that are currently captivating the fashion crowd. payload.text_excerpt: Vogue’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital | Vogue Skip to main content Your All Access Pass GET THE APP Travel Vogue ’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital By Talia Abbas February 6, 2025 Photo: Getty Images Save this story Save this story The legacy of the Antwerp Six looms large in the Belgian port city of the same name, drawing fashion obsessives from all over to explore the cobblestoned streets that the avant-garde collective of Dries Van Noten, Ann Demeulemeester, Dirk Van Saene, Walter Van Beirendonck, Dirk Bikkembergs, and Marina Yee once called home in the 1980s. And nearly four decades after the group’s debut, a new crop of influential designers is putting Antwerp back at the center of the fashion map, making it a must-visit for those eager to immerse themselves in the same artistic milieu. Pieter Mulier , Alaïa’s creative director, and Raf Simons , Prada’s co-creative director both consider Antwerp their home base. Matthieu Blazy , Chanel’s recently appointed artistic director, has also spent considerable time in Antwerp. But beyond the promise of a chance encounter with one of the industry’s leading names, the city is also home to up-and-coming labels—La Collection, Bernadette, and Julie Kegels —that are currently captivating the fashion crowd. Step 2: Adapt to the fragmented discovery journey

The new rules of multi-brand retail
Spotlight on: Francis Belin, CEO, Mytheresa*

payload.text_excerpt: How to Sell Now: Multi-Brand | Vogue Skip to main content Vogue Business is now in the Vogue App DOWNLOAD NOW Retail How to Sell Now: Multi-Brand By Vogue Business June 3, 2026 Photo: Getty Images / Artwork by Vogue Business Save this story Save this story As luxury brands double down on direct-to-consumer [DTC] , multi-brand retail is being pulled in two directions at once. On the one hand, wholesale remains essential for reach, discovery, and market entry — and our research shows it continues to play a meaningful role in conversion. On the other, it sits uneasily within an industry increasingly focused on controlling customer relationships, pricing, and experience. The result is a channel under pressure. Brands are reducing doors, renegotiating terms, and becoming far more selective about where and how they show up. Retailers, meanwhile, are being forced to evolve from scale-driven distributors into curators and cultural gatekeepers. “As brands prioritize direct-to-consumer, our value proposition is less about simply being a wholesale partner and more about being a highly strategic partner for discovery, brand elevation, and access to a very valuable customer base that is difficult for brands to acquire on their own,” says April Hennig, president of New York-based luxury retailer Moda Operandi. Moda Operandi was co-founded by Lauren Santo Domingo as a luxury e-commerce platform that allows shoppers to pre-order designer runway collections and shop curated in-season boutique

More Great Living Stories From Vogue
payload.text_excerpt: Vogue’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital | Vogue Skip to main content Your All Access Pass GET THE APP Travel Vogue ’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital By Talia Abbas February 6, 2025 Photo: Getty Images Save this story Save this story The legacy of the Antwerp Six looms large in the Belgian port city of the same name, drawing fashion obsessives from all over to explore the cobblestoned streets that the avant-garde collective of Dries Van Noten, Ann Demeulemeester, Dirk Van Saene, Walter Van Beirendonck, Dirk Bikkembergs, and Marina Yee once called home in the 1980s. And nearly four decades after the group’s debut, a new crop of influential designers is putting Antwerp back at the center of the fashion map, making it a must-visit for those eager to immerse themselves in the same artistic milieu. Pieter Mulier , Alaïa’s creative director, and Raf Simons , Prada’s co-creative director both consider Antwerp their home base. Matthieu Blazy , Chanel’s recently appointed artistic director, has also spent considerable time in Antwerp. But beyond the promise of a chance encounter with one of the industry’s leading names, the city is also home to up-and-coming labels—La Collection, Bernadette, and Julie Kegels —that are currently captivating the fashion crowd. Inside Antwerpen-Centraal station. Photo: Getty Images Located just 45 minutes by train from Brussels, the country’s second-largest city has always been the perfect place for a d

Pieter Mulier , Alaïa’s creative director, and Raf Simons , Prada’s co-creative director both consider Antwerp their home base. Matthieu Blazy , Chanel’s recently appointed artistic director, has also spent considerable time in Antwerp. But beyond the promise of a chance encounter with one of the industry’s leading names, the city is also home to up-and-coming labels—La Collection, Bernadette, and Julie Kegels —that are currently captivating the fashion crowd. payload.text_excerpt: How to Sell Now: Multi-Brand | Vogue Skip to main content Vogue Business is now in the Vogue App DOWNLOAD NOW Retail How to Sell Now: Multi-Brand By Vogue Business June 3, 2026 Photo: Getty Images / Artwork by Vogue Business Save this story Save this story As luxury brands double down on direct-to-consumer [DTC] , multi-brand retail is being pulled in two directions at once. On the one hand, wholesale remains essential for reach, discovery, and market entry — and our research shows it continues to play a meaningful role in conversion. On the other, it sits uneasily within an industry increasingly focused on controlling customer relationships, pricing, and experience. The result is a channel under pressure. Brands are reducing doors, renegotiating terms, and becoming far more selective about where and how they show up. Retailers, meanwhile, are being forced to evolve from scale-driven distributors into curators and cultural gatekeepers. “As brands prioritize direct-to-consumer, our value proposition is less about simply being a wholesale partner and more about being a highly strategic partner for discovery, brand elevation, and access to a very valuable customer base that is difficult for brands to acquire on their own,” says April Hennig, president of New York-based luxury retailer Moda Operandi. Fashion total like-for-like (LFL) sales rose +0.82%, according to the latest BDO High Street Sales Tracker, against a demanding +8.14% base a year earlier. Online did the heavy lifting. Non-store fashion jumped +10.24% against a strong +12.04% base — powerful growth on a tough comparison, and the first time since early summer that online has led the category. Fashion's online performance also far outpaced the wider online market, where total non-store sales rose just +1.05%. Store fashion, by contrast, fell -2.91%, against a demanding +8.63% base. The in-store channel that had anchored fashion throughout the summer took a step back, its decline set against an exceptionally strong week a year earlier and thinner store traffic this time round. Across the wider high street, total LFL sales rose +0.59% from a +6.31% base, helped by both channels. Total store sales grew +1.22%, extending their unbroken run, while total non-store sales rose +1.05%. Fashion's store weakness stood out against otherwise steady store trading elsewhere. It is a one-of-a-kind concept store that will become your only destination for all things slow fashion and slow living. It's an online marketplace (they also have a physical store in Goa) that expertly curates a list of brands, stylists, and designers who are contributing towards a sustainable future and eco-conscious living by creating pieces with great quality and organic materials that will last for years to come. You'll find several independent designers, brands, artisans, and makers who create an exquisite, contemporary, and absolutely unreal variety of fashion, art, jewellery, accessories, and home decor, with mindfulness at the centre. Think shirts, cover-ups, jewellery, skincare, and home decor, with myriad options of menswear (the Shima Kurta is lovely if you ask us) and kidswear ( Jungle Book Shirt is adorable) as well. payload.page_title: About Us – Blur The Border
payload.text_excerpt: About Us – Blur The Border Search for: Discover People Products Places Unblur Podcasts Debates India On The Map Events Campaign About Us Connect With Us About Us Blur The Border is a digital editorial platform that discovers and celebrates the powerhouses currently strengthening India’s homegrown landscape. We aim to bridge the gap between you and the artists shaping the cultural landscape of the country and pushing the boundaries of creativity, brands that are traditionally rooted but embrace global sensibilities, and places that offer immersive experiences. Through features, exclusive interviews, podcast series, curated offline events, and panel talks we aim to explore thought-provoking conversations. These span the subjects of art, design, fashion, and culture aiming to blur the borders between these creative disciplines. Backed by contributions from some of the most well-known names in India—including artists, entrepreneurs, stylists, designers, and more—our audience has evolved into a diverse community of creative thinkers and industry professionals since our inception. For those who seek to discover the country's best and beyond, or aspire to become part of it, this platform is for you. payload.text_excerpt: Vogue’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital | Vogue Skip to main content Your All Access Pass GET THE APP Travel Vogue ’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital By Talia Abbas February 6, 2025 Photo: Getty Images Save this story Save this story The legacy of the Antwerp Six looms large in the Belgian port city of the same name, drawing fashion obsessives from all over to explore the cobblestoned streets that the avant-garde collective of Dries Van Noten, Ann Demeulemeester, Dirk Van Saene, Walter Van Beirendonck, Dirk Bikkembergs, and Marina Yee once called home in the 1980s. And nearly four decades after the group’s debut, a new crop of influential designers is putting Antwerp back at the center of the fashion map, making it a must-visit for those eager to immerse themselves in the same artistic milieu. Pieter Mulier , Alaïa’s creative director, and Raf Simons , Prada’s co-creative director both consider Antwerp their home base. Matthieu Blazy , Chanel’s recently appointed artistic director, has also spent considerable time in Antwerp. But beyond the promise of a chance encounter with one of the industry’s leading names, the city is also home to up-and-coming labels—La Collection, Bernadette, and Julie Kegels —that are currently captivating the fashion crowd. payload.text_excerpt: Joan Smalls’ Tips for Good Shopping and Bargaining in India MENU JETSETTER'S GUIDE Joan Smalls’ Tips for Good Shopping and Bargaining in India The supermodel goes on a shopping adventure in Goa, India, and shares her tips for walking away with the best bargains. by Lauren McCarthy March 24, 2017 The first thing you notice when shopping with Joan Smalls is that she’s very decisive. Like a highly trained assassin, she’ll spot her prey immediately—in this case, a flowy, one-size-fits-all black and white striped sundress—make initial contact and then just yank it off the rack to hold it up against her 5’10 frame . Then it’s a careful dance—a stroll to take in the rest of the offerings, an occasional graze of another piece. But in the end, it’s that first piece that ends up leaving the store with the supermodel, destined for a life living amongst other, carefully selected (if not gifted directly from the designer personally) garments that live in her closet. It makes sense, once you think about it. Fashion has been Smalls’ domain for a decade, since she signed her first modeling contract. Over the past ten years, Smalls, who is originally from Puerto Rico, has emerged as one modeling’s biggest names , scoring endless magazine covers and advertising campaigns, a beauty contract with Estée Lauder, and, most recently, a gig as W Hotels (no relation to W magazine) first “Global Fashion Innovator,” a role which will see Smalls making plenty of trips to the hotel’s various properties ac

While, yes, you can find the typical goodies like elephant trousers, incense, and wall hangings, there are so many more cool, independent boutiques and designers in Goa getting their start! After all, while you can get those baggy, colorful elephant pants, how often can you really where them once you’re back home? Below is an insider list of places where you can find some really beautiful items, stuff to make your friends jealous. and stuff you will actually be able to wear once you return to your everyday life! Boutiques & Designers in Goa TIA Tia founded her namesake brand to offer a beautifully designed chic line of women’s swimwear and clothing. She’s a one woman entrepreneur who sources sustainable material and has everything made locally. Last season she had a beautiful shop in Mandrem – Alchemy – shared with Fara Boutique, though next year they are not sure if they will be going ahead with the space. Even if you haven’t made it to Goa yet, have a look at her website as she does international deliveries! If you are in Goa keep an eye and ear out for any Alchemy pop ups! Tia was one of Rachel’s best friends in Goa, so if you’ve ever wondered about what she was wearing in India , you’ve probably heard of this brand countless of times! Rangeela Rangeela, Assagao See On Map VISIT SITE Gunpowder's equally popular neighbour Rangeela is as much of a visual treat as it a treasure hunt. While you'll find a few curated brands here (think Baro, Chola The Label and more), a lot of finds are those that the owners have sourced from manufacturers across India and Indonesia. Together they set out to reshape the fashion industry for Indian women, building a diverse range of styles and collections from the ground up. In 2025, the brand stepped into a bold new chapter, refreshing its identity with a more global vision while staying true to the roots of creativity, inclusivity and style that defined it from the very beginning. The look evolved, but the mission stayed the same: to create apparel for women that complements their unique body shapes, personalities and preferences without compromising on aesthetic appeal. Every woman deserves to express her individuality through her clothing, and Miss Mosa is committed to making that vision a reality. Over the years, the brand has carved out a niche in the fashion world, becoming an essential part of every modern Indian woman's wardrobe. The dedication to crafting visually stunning and impeccably fitting clothing has earned an ever-growing fan base, with over 1.2 million loyal Instagram followers and counting. Miss Mosa is the epitome of style, substance and sustainability. Join us on this exhilarating journey as we continue to transform the world of fashion, one stunning outfit at a time. payload.text_excerpt: The Most Stylish Boutiques & Designers in Goa – Best Pixel Design Search Menu Cart 0 The Most Stylish Boutiques & Designers in Goa June 13, 2021 The shopping scene here is different to the rest of India. While, yes, you can find the typical goodies like elephant trousers, incense, and wall hangings, there are so many more cool, independent boutiques and designers in Goa getting their start! After all, while you can get those baggy, colorful elephant pants, how often can you really where them once you’re back home? Below is an insider list of places where you can find some really beautiful items, stuff to make your friends jealous. and stuff you will actually be able to wear once you return to your everyday life! Boutiques & Designers in Goa TIA Tia founded her namesake brand to offer a beautifully designed chic line of women’s swimwear and clothing. She’s a one woman entrepreneur who sources sustainable material and has everything made locally. Last season she had a beautiful shop in Mandrem – Alchemy – shared with Fara Boutique, though next year they are not sure if they will be going ahead with the space. Even if you haven’t made it to Goa yet, have a look at her website as she does international deliveries! If you are in Goa keep an eye and ear out for any Alchemy pop ups! Tia was one of Rachel’s best friends in Goa, so if you’ve ever wondered about what she was wearing in India , you’ve probably heard of this brand countless of times! SHOP HER WEBSITE & FOLLOW ON INSTAGRA

Space Tribe morphed into existance on the paradise beaches of Goa, India in the early 90's, a collaboration between brothers Olli & Miki Wisdom, & Richmond Headspace. Our aim? To turn our world into a tripped out circus party wonderland, based on Psy trance beats, our love of bright colours and optically twisted patterns, combined with the use of blacklights, a healthy dose of circus skills and just a pinch of Psychedelic! Normal is Boring We were blasting at the parties & high on life, loving the pulse of the emerging psy trance music scene. But the clothes we wanted to wear, that celebrated our individuality & our joy of life didn't exist. Somehow, a pair of jeans & a benetton t-shirt didn't come close. Created in Chaos Off to Bali where we made a few dozen pieces of very colourful clothes & some funky batik banners for ourselves and a few friends. Upon our return to Goa we discovered many people were inspired & wanted a piece of the action too, so our personal production turned into a small scale business. We soon developed & refined our own particular style of flouro madness. . . And thus, the Tribe was born. We are all made of stars Our inspiration is drawn from psychedelic trance parties

payload.text_excerpt: 76 Multi-Brand Retailers Worth Knowing Subscribe Sign in 76 Multi-Brand Retailers Worth Knowing Where to find the most interesting mix of brands, around the world. Angharad Jones Best Apr 16, 2026 ∙ Paid 43 3 Share Earlier this year, I wrote the small and independent brand index : a list that currently stands at 138 womenswear brands that are, you guessed it, small and/or independent. I wanted to shine a light on the brands that are doing things differently and offering something beyond the usual. It’s my most popular post to date, so it turns out you lot are craving that, too. On the back of that, I started to think about all the multi-brand retailers where I quite often unearth these brands. The usual suspects online (hello, Net-a-Porter ), but also the small ones in residential neighbourhoods or in places you wouldn’t think to look. Where the owners know their customers by their first names, and where you can find the kinds of brands that are hard to come by elsewhere. So, welcome to the multi-brand retailer index. Some are online-only, while most have a physical and online presence, and most have both men’s and women’s wear. The UK list is heavy, as that’s where I've spent most of my life, but there are also plenty of entries for mainland Europe, North America, and Australia & New Zealand (big thanks to the subscribers in my chat who contributed their favourites!). Victoria Kim By Victoria Kim The fashion industry has undergone rapid change in the past three years. We have witnessed fast-fashion retailing followed by a sudden prominence of SPA brands, and now we have an emergence of multi-brand select shops where fashion and lifestyle coexist together. We have also seen a change in retailing from online stores to offline. For example, Style Nanda, an online shopping mall, has opened an off-line store on the strength of its online business. In China, there is a growing demand of spot stores which cover hot fashion trends in each region. It means that select shops are becoming diversified and offer both online and off line services to customers. Multi-shop is not a new notion. Its retailing identity simply has been evolving from individual product and merchandising-based to B2C communications. This change derives from concerns over how to communicate better with customers. Monocle examines its success as it celebrates its first decade. Writers Tyler Brûlé Irene Lam Photographer Julie Mayfeng Share Copied! For department store CEOs, architects and bank analysts, the annual global retail inspiration/research tour still throws up the same predictable itinerary: one day in London, one in Paris, a possible side trip to see what’s going on in Berlin, a touch-and-go in Milan, Dubai (optional), Mumbai (optional), Hong Kong one day but two nights so there’s spa time at the Mandarin, and then two full days in Tokyo. If Monocle were doing the bookings we’d take a few detours and visit Coccodrillo’s new shop in Antwerp, alight in Beirut to snap up some inexpensive shop space and then do a full two days in Seoul. While Antwerp has long been a favourite destination for getting ideas and Beirut continues to boom thanks to Solidere’s redevelopment of the city centre (Hermès and Louis Vuitton have both launched stores over the past few weeks), Seoul is still a bit of a mystery. But over the past decade, something else has quietly evolved. Luxury shopping in Goa has grown into its own experience, one that feels curated, design-led, and deeply connected to the state’s slower coastal rhythm. This isn’t mall culture. It isn’t high-street chaos. And it’s definitely not flea-market bargaining. It's a boutique. It’s thoughtful, and it’s built for people who like discovering pieces, not just buying them. If you’re looking for luxury shopping in Goa, here’s what you should expect and where to go. What This Guide Covers (And What It Doesn’t) This blog focuses on: Premium boutiques Designer resort wear Artisanal studios Elevated home décor spaces Lifestyle concept stores It does not cover flea markets or street shopping Luxury retail in Goa operates differently. It’s intimate. It’s often appointment-based. And it’s built around experience, not volume. How Luxury Retail in Goa Evolved Goa wasn’t always known for boutique retail. The shift began when second-home buyers, designers, artists, and long-stay travellers started spending extended time here. They weren’t looking for fast fashion. They were looking for craftsmanship. And nearly four decades after the group’s debut, a new crop of influential designers is putting Antwerp back at the center of the fashion map, making it a must-visit for those eager to immerse themselves in the same artistic milieu. Pieter Mulier , Alaïa’s creative director, and Raf Simons , Prada’s co-creative director both consider Antwerp their home base. Matthieu Blazy , Chanel’s recently appointed artistic director, has also spent considerable time in Antwerp. But beyond the promise of a chance encounter with one of the industry’s leading names, the city is also home to up-and-coming labels—La Collection, Bernadette, and Julie Kegels —that are currently captivating the fashion crowd. Fashion total like-for-like (LFL) sales rose +0.82%, according to the latest BDO High Street Sales Tracker, against a demanding +8.14% base a year earlier. Online did the heavy lifting. Non-store fashion jumped +10.24% against a strong +12.04% base — powerful growth on a tough comparison, and the first time since early summer that online has led the category. Fashion's online performance also far outpaced the wider online market, where total non-store sales rose just +1.05%. Store fashion, by contrast, fell -2.91%, against a demanding +8.63% base. The in-store channel that had anchored fashion throughout the summer took a step back, its decline set against an exceptionally strong week a year earlier and thinner store traffic this time round. Across the wider high street, total LFL sales rose +0.59% from a +6.31% base, helped by both channels. Total store sales grew +1.22%, extending their unbroken run, while total non-store sales rose +1.05%. Fashion's store weakness stood out against otherwise steady store trading elsewhere. payload.text_excerpt: Vogue’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital | Vogue Skip to main content Your All Access Pass GET THE APP Travel Vogue ’s Guide to Antwerp, Belgium’s Long-Standing Fashion Capital By Talia Abbas February 6, 2025 Photo: Getty Images Save this story Save this story The legacy of the Antwerp Six looms large in the Belgian port city of the same name, drawing fashion obsessives from all over to explore the cobblestoned streets that the avant-garde collective of Dries Van Noten, Ann Demeulemeester, Dirk Van Saene, Walter Van Beirendonck, Dirk Bikkembergs, and Marina Yee once called home in the 1980s. And nearly four decades after the group’s debut, a new crop of influential designers is putting Antwerp back at the center of the fashion map, making it a must-visit for those eager to immerse themselves in the same artistic milieu. Pieter Mulier , Alaïa’s creative director, and Raf Simons , Prada’s co-creative director both consider Antwerp their home base. Matthieu Blazy , Chanel’s recently appointed artistic director, has also spent considerable time in Antwerp. But beyond the promise of a chance encounter with one of the industry’s leading names, the city is also home to up-and-coming labels—La Collection, Bernadette, and Julie Kegels —that are currently captivating the fashion crowd. payload.text_excerpt: Joan Smalls’ Tips for Good Shopping and Bargaining in India MENU JETSETTER'S GUIDE Joan Smalls’ Tips for Good Shopping and Bargaining in India The supermodel goes on a shopping adventure in Goa, India, and shares her tips for walking away with the best bargains. by Lauren McCarthy March 24, 2017 The first thing you notice when shopping with Joan Smalls is that she’s very decisive. Like a highly trained assassin, she’ll spot her prey immediately—in this case, a flowy, one-size-fits-all black and white striped sundress—make initial contact and then just yank it off the rack to hold it up against her 5’10 frame . Then it’s a careful dance—a stroll to take in the rest of the offerings, an occasional graze of another piece. But in the end, it’s that first piece that ends up leaving the store with the supermodel, destined for a life living amongst other, carefully selected (if not gifted directly from the designer personally) garments that live in her closet. It makes sense, once you think about it. Fashion has been Smalls’ domain for a decade, since she signed her first modeling contract.
